description: Turn a place (address, POI, town) into coordinates. Ask two ways, and they combine: `query` is free text — one run-together string, the way a person types into a search box — and `street`, `housenumber`, `city`, `postcode` and `country` name the parts of an address separately. At least one of the two is required. Pass the parts whenever you already hold the address in parts (a form, a CRM row, a manifest): components are REQUIREMENTS, not hints, so `city: "London"` means a result outside London cannot come back at all, where "London" inside `query` only reorders. `country` takes an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code or a country name ("GB", "United Kingdom"); a value naming no country is refused rather than silently matching nothing. Returns up to `limit` (default 10) candidates with name, one-line label, lat/lon, type and address parts. Pass `focus` {lat, lon} to rank results near a location higher. A bare city or town name (no comma) lists that city's airports and main railway stations directly behind it, ahead of namesakes elsewhere. Each hit also carries `match`: a per-component matched/inferred/unmatched verdict, the `score_gap` to the runner-up, and which backend answered. READ IT before acting on an address — an unmatched or inferred postcode on the top hit means the answer does not carry the address you asked for, and a small `score_gap` means the ranking barely chose, so show the alternatives instead of picking one. Use `verify_places` when the address came from a model or a user and needs checking rather than using. Results are matched in `lang` (default "en"), so English exonyms — "Munich", "Cologne", "Geneva" — resolve to the place meant; pass `lang` when querying in another language, or "default" for each place's local name.

LatLon.description: A WGS84 coordinate in decimal degrees: a {lat, lon} object (preferred), or a GeoJSON [lon, lat] array with LONGITUDE FIRST, the same order as every polygon field on this server.

city.description:
Structured component: town or city, e.g. "London". Matches the
containing city as well as the immediate locality, so a suburb name
works here too.

country.description:
Structured component: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code or country name —
"GB", "gb", "United Kingdom" and "UK" all mean the same country.
A value naming no country is refused rather than quietly applied as
a filter that matches nothing.

focus.description: Optional location bias: results near this point rank higher.

housenumber.description:
Structured component: house number, e.g. "10" or "221B". Only
meaningful alongside `street` — a house number on its own excludes
nearly everything and identifies nothing.

lang.description:
Language of the place names to match and return, as a two-letter
code. Defaults to "en", which is what makes English exonyms
("Munich", "Cologne", "Geneva") resolve to the place meant rather
than a same-named town elsewhere. Set it to the language your
query is written in; "default" asks for each place's own local
name. Deployments support a fixed set (this one: "en", "de",
"fr"), and anything outside it is refused.

postcode.description:
Structured component: postcode in any spacing or case — "SW1A 2AA"
and "sw1a2aa" are one query. A bare UK outward code ("SW1A")
selects the whole district.

query.description:
Free-text place query, e.g. "Dover ferry terminal". Required unless
at least one structured component is supplied.

street.description:
Structured component: street name, e.g. "Downing Street". Matches
the street of addresses and POIs (transliterated street names
included) as well as the street itself.

name: geocode

label.description: Human-readable one-line label assembled from the address parts.

match.description:
How far this hit can be trusted to be the place that was asked
for — see [`GeocodeMatch`]. Present whenever the MapMap gateway
answered; absent on a deployment falling back to the direct Photon
geocoder, and absent on the gateway's own fast paths (a pasted
coordinate pair, a bare UK outward code, a category browse), which
answer without a ranking to report on.

name.description: Place name, when the source feature has one.

type.description:
Feature type, e.g. "house", "street", "city" (falls back to the
OSM value when the endpoint does not classify).

GeocodeMatch.description:
How well one geocoding result answers what was actually asked.

Geocoding's real failure mode is not "no answer" but a confident answer
to a different question: a plausible row on the wrong street, with
nothing in the response to say so. This object is that missing say-so,
and an agent should read it before acting on an address.

How to read it:

* Any component `unmatched` or `inferred` on the TOP hit means the
  answer does not carry the address that was asked for — an `unmatched`
  postcode means the result has no postcode at all, `inferred` means it
  has a different one. Neither is a match. Say so rather than presenting
  the hit as the address, and reach for `verify_places` when the address
  came from a model or a user and needs checking rather than using.
* A small `score_gap` means the ranking barely chose between this hit
  and the runner-up, which is exactly when to show the alternatives
  instead of picking one for the user.

components.description:
Per-component verdict on this hit: one entry for each structured
component supplied, and empty when the query was free text only.

score_gap.description:
The top result's score minus the runner-up's, rounded to 3 decimal
places. `0` for a single result, and `0` from the `photon` source,
which publishes no per-result score — so a `0` is "no signal", not
"a tie".

source.description:
Which backend answered: "mapmap-index" (the first-party index) or
"photon".

GeocodeMatchComponents.description:
Per-component verdicts inside a [`GeocodeMatch`]. Each is one of
"matched", "inferred" or "unmatched"; a component that was not supplied
is absent entirely.

* "matched" — the result's own field carries the value asked for (case-
  and accent-insensitive, and by containment, so `city: "London"`
  matches "City of London").
* "inferred" — the result carries a value for that component, but not
  the one asked for. It reached the page through ranking, as when a
  street is found by its transliterated name and displayed under its
  canonical one.
* "unmatched" — the result carries no value for that component at all.
